verdict.rationale: Appwrite documents an official MCP server, including a hosted one, that lets LLMs interact directly with its API. It also ships first-party plugins so agents like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Claude Desktop can operate on an Appwrite project (projects, rows, files, users, functions) after an OAuth sign-in. Natural-language operation therefore works, but only through an external AI client: there is no evidence of a native natural-language interface in the Console or CLI, and no hands-on reports of how well it works. Missing for 10: a native in-product natural-language command interface, independent or hands-on corroboration of agent-driven operation, and documentation of which operations the MCP tools cover or exclude.
